sentences.text:
The appellant has been arrested on 04-03-2024 relating to Crime No.86 of 2024 registered at Police Station Kampoo, District Gwalior (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 366, 376, 342, 294,
506 of IPC and Sections 3 (1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(va) of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
As per the case of prosecution case, father of prosecutrix reported to Police Station Kampoo, District Gwalior that his daughter aged around 20 years is missing since afternoon of 01.03.2024.
Police Station Kampoo registered Missing Person Report No.16/2024.
Prosecutrix appeared before Police Station Kampoo, District Gwalior on 03.03.2024 along with her parents.
In her statement recorded under Section 161 of CrPC, prosecutrix alleged that Shyam Gurjar took her to house of some unknown person in his Scorpio vehicle.
There, Shyam Gurjar committed rape on her and abused her with reference to her caste.
Appellant kept her confined for two days in that house.

On 03.03.2024,
appellant left her near Police Station Jhansi Road, Gwalior.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 of CrPC, prosecutrix alleged that three other unknown boys were associate of Shyam Gurjar.
But later, in her supplementary statement recorded on 03.04.2024, she resiled from the statement and stated that no other boy was involved in the alleged incident.
Appellant was arrested on 04.03.2024.
He is in custody ever since.
Investigation is underway.

Learned Counsel for the appellant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the appeal, submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in this matter due to pressure of the family members of the prosecutrix.
It is a case of romantic relationship between two consenting adults.
The prosecutrix left her parental home at her own and went with the accused.
After returning home, she had made false allegation against the appellant.
She is constantly changing the allegation on advice of family members.
Learned counsel submits that appellant is aged around 19 years and is Contractor by profession.
No offence as alleged is made against the appellant.
No criminal antecedent is reported against him.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family, home and profession.
No custodial interrogation is required against the appellant.
There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence.
Investigation and trial would take time to conclude.

On these grounds, learned counsel prays that learned Special Judge has committed an error in rejecting the application for bail,
therefore, the impugned order be set aside and appellant may be extended the benefit of bail.
P er contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the appeal on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case regard being had to the young age of the appellant, while setting aside order dated 21-03-2024 passed by Trial Court, this Court is inclined to release the appellant on bail.
Thus, the appeal is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that the appellant Shyam Gurjar s hall be released on bail in relation to Crime No.86 of 2024 registered at Police Station Kampoo, District Gwalior (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 366, 376, 342, 294, 506 of IPC and Sections 3 (1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(va) of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with one solvent surety of the Shyam Gurjar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134026929/
